The Silent Predator and the Majestic Prey - Snow Leopard and Markhor
questions: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
The Rasoolullah (PBUH) was born in Makkah Mukarramah.
In pre-Islamic Arabia, the Arabs' eloquence and memory found expression in:
The Arabs had remarkable memory and eloquence, which found expression in poetry.
At which place was a yearly fair held for poetical competitions?
Every year a fair was held for poetical competitions at Ukaz.
At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) begin spending most of his time in solitude and meditation?
When he was thirty-eight he spent most of his time in solitude and meditation.
In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meditate?
He used to retire to the cave of Hira with food and water to remember Allah.
Which angel brought the first revelation?
Hazrat Jibril came to him in the cave of Hira with Allah's message.
The first revealed verses begin with the command:
Read in the name of thy Lord
'Read in the name of thy Lord Who created...' (Quran 96:1-5).
For how many years did the revelation continue?
The revelation continued for the next twenty-three years.
Solitude is the state of being alone, especially when you find it pleasant.
Love for the motherland or devotion to one's country
Patriotism means love for the motherland or devotion to one's country.
The word 'patriot' comes from the Latin word:
It comes from the Latin word 'patriota', which means countryman.
According to the text, the supreme values for a patriot are:
sovereignty, integrity and honour of the country
For a patriot, the sovereignty, integrity and honour of the country are supreme values.
Who led the Muslims of the subcontinent in their struggle for a separate homeland?
Quaid-e-Azam secured a separate homeland for the Muslims.
In which wars did many brave soldiers lay down their lives for Pakistan, according to the text?
Many soldiers laid down their lives in the wars of 1965, 1971 and Kargil.
'Patriotism is a commendable quality' is a statement of:
It expresses a judgement, so it is an opinion; facts can be proved with evidence.
The cause is why something happens; the effect is:
The cause is why something happens, and the effect is what happens as a result.
In the first line, the poet compares himself to a:
'I wandered lonely as a cloud' — a simile comparing himself to a cloud.
Where did the poet see the daffodils?
Beside the lake, beneath the trees
'Beside the lake, beneath the trees, fluttering and dancing in the breeze.'
How many daffodils did the poet see at a glance?
'Ten thousand saw I at a glance, tossing their heads in sprightly dance.'
The daffodils are compared to stars that shine on the:
'Continuous as the stars that shine and twinkle on the milky way.'
When do the daffodils flash upon the poet's 'inward eye'?
When he lies in vacant or pensive mood
'For oft, when on my couch I lie in vacant or in pensive mood, they flash upon that inward eye.'
'Fluttering and dancing in the breeze' gives the daffodils human qualities. This is called:
Giving human actions like dancing to flowers is personification.
The 'inward eye' in the poem refers to:
The inward eye is the mind's memory, 'the bliss of solitude'.
In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madinah?
He migrated with Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique to Madinah in 622 A.D.
Hazrat Asma (RA) was the daughter of:
Hazrat Asma was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique.
Which title did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) give Hazrat Asma (RA)?
For tying the food with her own belt, she was given the title of (Zat-un-)Nitaqain.
Why was Hazrat Asma (RA) given this title?
She tied the food on the camel with her own belt
She tied the food on the camel's back with her own belt as nothing else could be found.
In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr hide during the migration?
Hazrat Asma secretly carried food every night to the cave of Thawr.
Who slapped Hazrat Asma (RA) when she would not tell where her father was?
Abu Jehl slapped her so hard that her ear-ring fell off, but she did not reveal the secret.
What did Hazrat Asma (RA) reply when Abu Jehl asked 'Where is your father?'
She wisely replied with a counter question, 'How would I know?'
Hazrat Asma's grandfather, Hazrat Abu Quhafa, was:
Her grandfather Hazrat Abu Quhafa was very old and blind.
Which prominent businesswoman of Makkah is given as an early example of a woman entrepreneur?
Hazrat Khadija was a prominent businesswoman known for wisdom, integrity and leadership.
starting and running a business, taking financial risks for profit
Entrepreneurship means starting and running a business, taking on financial risks and seeking profit.
What do Microfinance Institutions offer to women in Pakistan?
Microfinance institutions offer loans to help women start small businesses.
Which is a challenge for women entrepreneurs mentioned in the lesson?
Traditional gender roles that prioritise household duties create barriers for women.
What provides platforms for female entrepreneurs to network and showcase products?
Women's chambers of commerce provide platforms to network and showcase products.
The story of Hazrat Khadija shows that:
gender should not be a barrier to success
She became a symbol of empowerment, showing gender should not be a barrier to success.
Despite his good qualities, he was terribly weak in managing his time.
How did Taseer waste his time?
He spent hours on video games, chatting with friends and daydreaming.
Who decided to teach Taseer a lesson about time?
His grandfather, a wise old man, decided to impart a valuable lesson.
What was in the basket the grandfather showed Taseer?
There was an empty jar and a basket with big rocks, pebbles and sand.
Why could Taseer not fit the big rocks into the jar?
He put the sand and pebbles in first
He poured in sand and pebbles first, leaving no room for the big rocks.
What did the grandfather put into the jar first?
He placed the big rocks first, then pebbles, then sand filled the gaps.
The big rocks in the jar stand for:
the most important tasks in life
The lesson: put important tasks first; smaller things fit around them.
delaying tasks that should be done
Procrastination is putting off work, as Taseer did, until it piles up.
Which famous book was written by Rudyard Kipling?
Kipling is best known for works such as The Jungle Book, Kim and The Man Who Would Be King.
He was born in the British colonial subcontinent, which influenced much of his writing.
According to the poem, Triumph and Disaster should be treated as:
'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster and treat those two impostors just the same.'
'If you can keep your head when all about you are losing theirs' means:
Keeping your head means staying calm and sensible when others panic.
'If you can dream — and not make dreams your ___'
'If you can dream — and not make dreams your master.'
qualities of a balanced and mature person
The poem lists qualities like patience, honesty and self-control that make a person mature.
In 'neither... nor', 'not only... but also', the words are called:
Pairs like neither/nor and not only/but also are correlative conjunctions.
In 'He could not attend the meeting because he was sick', 'because' is a:
'Because' joins a dependent clause to an independent clause: a subordinating conjunction.
Which products does Pakistan export, according to the lesson?
We export textiles, rice and sports goods to countries all over the world.
Which initiative is mentioned as bringing foreign direct investment to Pakistan?
Foreign direct investment, especially through CPEC, brings capital and technology.
Advances in technology, transportation and communication
Advances in technology, transport and communication have accelerated globalisation.
How has digital globalisation helped students?
They can learn about different cultures through websites and videos
Students can learn about cultures, traditions and histories through websites, videos and articles.
Social media interaction between cultures promotes:
Seeing how others live and celebrate helps promote empathy.
Jobs created by multinational companies in Pakistan often offer:
These jobs often offer better pay and working conditions than local companies.
According to the lesson, education fosters economic growth, reduces poverty and promotes:
Education fosters growth, reduces poverty, promotes gender equality and helps protect the environment.
Which subjects help students develop critical thinking and problem-solving?
Mathematics, science and technology develop critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
the knowledge, skills and health people accumulate
Human capital is the knowledge, skills and health individuals accumulate over their lives.
By preparing students for industries, quality education reduces unemployment and underemployment.
Quality education acts as a 'leveller', meaning it:
It provides equal opportunities for all, regardless of socio-economic background.
Which skills does quality education emphasise for employability?
Literacy, numeracy, digital literacy and vocational skills
These skills enhance employability and economic independence.
The snow leopard is often called the:
The snow leopard is often referred to as the 'Ghost of the Mountains'.
Up to what altitude does the snow leopard roam?
It roams at altitudes as high as 5,500 metres.
How do the snow leopard's long tails help it?
Their long tails help them balance on narrow ledges.
The markhor's horns are shaped like a:
The markhor has impressive corkscrew-shaped horns.
'Markhor' means 'snake-eater' in Persian, referring to horns like coiled snakes.
The markhor is a herbivore feeding on grasses, shrubs and leaves.
The snow leopard and the markhor are a classic example of:
Snow leopards rely on markhors for food — a classic predator-prey relationship.
If the snow leopard disappeared, according to the lesson:
it would create a ripple effect harming the ecosystem
As a top predator it keeps the balance; its loss would cause a ripple effect.
Who wrote the one-act play 'The Dear Departed'?
'The Dear Departed' is by William Stanley Houghton (1881-1913).
Who is Mr. Abel Merryweather in the play?
Father of Amelia Slater and Elizabeth Jordan
Abel Merryweather is the father of Amelia Slater and Elizabeth Jordan, and grandfather of Victoria.
Victoria Slater is the daughter of:
Victoria is the daughter of Amelia and Henry Slater.
Where is the whole play set?
In the living room of the Slater family's house
The play's sole location is the living room of the Slaters' house.
Which items do the Slaters secretly take from grandfather's room?
Mrs. Slater and Henry carry down grandfather's bureau and take his clock.
Mrs. Slater tells Victoria not to tell her aunt about the:
'Victoria, don't breathe a word to your aunt about the clock and the bureau.'
a single act, focused plot and limited characters
A one-act play unfolds in one act with a straightforward plot, few characters and one setting.
The play 'The Dear Departed' mainly criticises:
The daughters' rush to divide their father's belongings exposes greed and selfishness.
